method.coverageBoundary: This is not a new full-repository semantic audit. The complete 1941-file SHA pass proves unchanged bytes outside three cumulative CI/test files relative to audit5; no broader new semantic review is claimed.

conclusions: The raw CI assertion was onSaved callback expected once/actual zero at original test line 535. It did not directly measure a zero total update-call count.

Recovery persists accepted via reconcileOperation, which emits a changed event after the storage transaction. useOperations separately awaits listOperations before publishing its React snapshot. The form may display the retained-draft notice while its older unknown operation still disables saving.

The new spy calls the original listOperations and only delays returning real accepted records for the same original operation ID. It neither fabricates receipt success nor bypasses the IndexedDB transaction or production admission gate. Observing the real unknown read and holding the accepted read makes the conservative UI transition explicit.

Before release the test requires save disabled, a click leaves exactly the first automation/update call, and onSaved remains uncalled. The explicit newer-record conflict and rebase are preserved; rebase still clears confirmation and the user confirms again.

After releasing the read, the existing enabledButton helper waits for the visible control to become enabled without retrying mutation. The test requires exactly two total update calls, one onSaved callback, original receipt operation ID, expectedRevision 6 and the retained Review my project text.

Other positive save clicks use the existing readiness helper. No skip, retry, arbitrary sleep, timeout increase, removed behavioral assertion, production change or synthetic accepted receipt was introduced by this patch.
